measures.measure_id: CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT - REQUIRE PHOTO ID FOR VOTING
match: CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT - REQUIRE PHOTO ID FOR VOTING
Require Photo ID for All Voters

official_title.value: CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT - REQUIRE PHOTO ID FOR VOTING

official_summary.value: This amendment to the North Carolina Constitution would require presentation of photographic identification for voters in all instances in North Carolina elections.
official_summary.by: Legislative Services Officer, N.C. General Assembly (G.S. 147-54.10), adopted August 20, 2026

full_text.value: Constitutional amendment to require all voters, not just those presenting to vote in person, to present photo identification before voting.

placed_by.detail: Referred by the North Carolina General Assembly (Session Law 2024-58)

unsourced: official_title: NC does not number amendments; value is the contest name in the State Board of Elections referendum list, identical to the contest name in the live results feed (er.ncsbe.gov). The Legislative Services Officer's caption is "Require Photo ID for All Voters".

legislative_vote: third-reading roll calls (Senate roll call #677 on 12/2/2024 (https://www.ncleg.gov/Legislation/Votes/RollCallVoteTranscript/2023/S/677); House roll call #810 on 12/11/2024 (https://www.ncleg.gov/Legislation/Votes/RollCallVoteTranscript/2023/H/810)).

official_summary: the Legislative Services Officer's summary explanation was read from the copy posted by the Forsyth County Board of Elections (official county election office); no copy was found on ncleg.gov or ncsbe.gov.

opposition_committee_name: no referendum committee registered with the NC State Board of Elections as opposing this amendment was found; the NCSBE committee lookup (cf.ncsbe.gov) is a name search only and cannot list committees by ballot measure. None recorded.
proponent_website / opposition_website: none found on an official source.
party_positions: no position from the North Carolina Republican Party found on nc.gop.

legislative_vote.by_party: counted from the party-grouped member lists on the ncleg.gov roll call transcripts. In the House the Republican "Ayes" list includes the Speaker, so the per-party ayes add up to one more than the official "Ayes" total; yes/no/other use the official totals.
